title: A jump on a wide edit shows its picture whole, and Space with it starts sooner
goal: Clicking somewhere new on a paused 50 track edit draws the new place in pieces, some clips missing until each is read, and Space pressed in the same instant waits a quarter to half a second. A jump should show the new place once, whole, and playing from it should follow as fast as it can.
notes: Reproduced 2026-11-25: walk with setup {forget:[all],wideEdit:50}, steps speed pictures fromMS 10000 (and 62000) when [atOnce]: 5 nothing drawn at 0:10.0, 10 at 1:02.0, both in the one picture the jump itself submits (scrubDocument -> documentMomentChanged -> submit). speed starts when [atOnce] gives the waits. The wait is decoding: skipped/decoded counts per clip showed 30 to 110 samples from the key frame each, few of them skippable, about 600 a second on one decoder. Ideas not tried: hold the picture on a paused jump the way holdsPictureForStart does; small all-intra stand-ins kept per recording.
acceptance: A jump while paused on the 50 track edit hands the canvas no picture with a clip missing or from another time (today 5 missing at 0:10, 10 at 1:02)
Space in the same instant as a jump: first moving picture stated before and after at 0:10, 0:30, 0:58 and 1:02 (today 545, 266, 230 and 409 ms), and lower at each
The starts held by play-starts-at-once-on-a-wide-edit-walk do not grow, and a scrub still shows a picture on every move

log.note: Triage 2026-11-26: moved to p1 with the rest of the wide edit report. Clips missing from the picture after a jump is the 'no frame shows a blank or a stale picture' line of the focus, and a person clicking around a 50 track edit sees it.

Possibly related, unmeasured: on the scrub task (pass 4, 2026-11-26) starting an AVAudioEngine at the press held the window server up about 40 ms later for 12-22 ms (main thread blocked in mach_msg send inside CA::Context::commit_transaction), fixed there by starting the scrub engine before the drag. DocumentAudioEngine starts the output at Space the same way, so Space's first frames may pay the same hold; worth a look when timing starts.
